plotSections.title: Gerk and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: Gerk is explicitly confirmed as the chosen child foretold by the Mother's Prayer, though the prophecy does not determine his choices or how he arrived at this point.
The Mother's Prayer is an ancient prophecy sacred to the Navi. It describes a recurring pattern of catastrophic events, a hero rising from them, and that hero eventually facing difficult choices.
The prophecy has appeared in multiple journals or tomes written by different authors, and the Mother's Tales have sometimes changed or rewritten themselves.
The Mother's Prayer is compared to a fruiting tree: the prophecy is the tree, while the chosen hero is a fruit produced by it.
The great tree has diminished over the years and is approaching another growth cycle. A new 'bud' is expected when the current growing season ends.

Gerk is being offered the choice to consciously take up the role foretold by the Mother's Prayer rather than simply continuing along his existing path. He agrees to pursue the role if doing so will help Atlas.
The DM states that no son or daughter of the Mother's Prayer has stepped forward to take up the role in roughly 1,500 years.

The DM explains that Gerk's decision also affects his companions. They may voluntarily join him as part of his entourage and become metaphorical siblings or relatives of the chosen child of the Great Tree.
Dana chooses to follow Gerk, stating that if he has been chosen there must be a purpose and that she will go wherever he goes.
Walker and the others appear willing to participate, though the exact nature of their relationship to the Great Tree and Gerk's role is still being explained.

Gerk asks about Daisy, the small girl who has repeatedly appeared around him and is associated with flowers. The DM has not personally encountered or identified Daisy and does not provide an explanation for her identity.
Gerk states that Daisy has previously stopped time without anyone else noticing, reinforcing that she may be an unusual or supernatural presence connected to his story.

chronologicalEvents: The DM challenges Gerk to consider whether he is prepared to accept greater responsibility if he truly is the chosen figure of the Mother's Prayer.
The DM confirms that Gerk is the chosen child foretold by the Mother's Prayer and explains the prophecy's history among the Navi.
The Mother's Prayer is described as a recurring prophetic story involving catastrophe, a hero, and increasingly difficult choices for that hero.
The DM explains that the prophecy does not dictate Gerk's actions; his choices have remained his own, and the prophetic accounts can apparently change or rewrite themselves.
The DM reveals that Gerk is one of the sons and daughters of the Great Tree and that no such chosen child has taken up the role in approximately 1,500 years.
Gerk agrees to accept guidance and pursue the role if doing so can help Atlas.
The DM explains that Gerk's companions may voluntarily join him as part of his entourage and become metaphorical brothers and sisters of the chosen child of the Great Tree.
Walker learns that Gerk is a chosen child and that the Great Tree is connected to the Mother's Prayer.
The party discusses the strange significance of the role and realizes that Gerk's companions may also become connected to the Great Tree through him.
Dana formally states that she will follow Gerk wherever he goes because his selection implies a greater purpose.
Gerk asks whether the party understands who Daisy is; the DM says he has never seen her and cannot explain her identity.
Gerk recalls that Daisy, a small girl, has previously stopped time without anyone else noticing.

notes: Explicitly confirmed to be the chosen child foretold by the Mother's Prayer.
Is described as a son of the Great Tree and one of the rare children produced by the Mother's Prayer.
Chooses to take up the role associated with the Mother's Prayer after being told that doing so could help all of Atlas.
His choices are still his own; the prophecy describes and anticipates his path but does not dictate his decisions.
The DM says Gerk's decision has consequences for his companions, who may voluntarily join him as part of his entourage.
Gerk continues to question the certainty of the prophecy and asks how he can know that its description uniquely identifies him.
Gerk has repeatedly encountered a small girl named Daisy, who has apparently demonstrated supernatural abilities.
titles: Chosen Child of the Mother's Prayer
personality: Initially reluctant to seek a greater destiny and prefers continuing his existing life with his friends.
Accepts greater responsibility when he believes it can help Atlas.
quotesThemes: Gerk's recurring attitude is that he is happiest simply doing his thing with his friends.
He questions whether the prophecy is specific enough to distinguish him from other possible candidates.
openQuestions: What exactly is the role Gerk is expected to fulfill as the chosen child?
What difficult choices does the Mother's Prayer foretell for Gerk?
What will happen when the Mother's Prayer's current growing season ends and the next bud appears?

notes: An ancient sacred prophecy of the Navi describing a recurring cycle involving catastrophe, a hero, and difficult choices.
The prophecy is compared to a fruiting tree, with the chosen hero represented as a fruit growing from the tree.
Multiple journals or tomes contain versions of the Mother's Prayer, with different authors recording the story.
The prophetic accounts can apparently rewrite themselves under certain circumstances, particularly when a son or daughter of the tree chooses their own path.
The prophecy has explicitly identified Gerk as its current chosen child.
The DM says the prophecy originated in the early history of the Navi in Midgard and Atlas.
The Mother's Prayer is also referred to as the Mother's Tales.
quotesThemes: The prophecy concerns a catastrophic event, the rise of a hero, and increasingly difficult choices made by that hero.
The prophecy describes a path without necessarily forcing the individual to follow it.
openQuestions: Who originally gave or authored the Mother's Prayer?
Who or what determines when the next chosen child appears?

Great Eldarin Tree.existing: The sacred Great Eldarin Tree is associated with the origins of the keystones and the Navi.
notes: The Great Tree is directly connected to the Mother's Prayer and its chosen children.
The chosen individuals are described as sons and daughters of the Great Tree.
The DM describes the Mother's Prayer itself as the tree and the chosen individual as a fruit produced by it.
The tree has diminished over the years and is currently approaching the end of a growing season.
A new bud is expected to appear when the current growing season ends.
The party may become metaphorical brothers and sisters of Gerk through his relationship to the Great Tree.
quotesThemes: The Great Tree represents an ongoing source or lineage of chosen heroes rather than a single historical individual.
openQuestions: What exactly causes the Great Tree to produce a new chosen child?
What does the next bud signify?

Navi.existing: Ancient race associated with the Great Eldarin Tree and keystones.
notes: The Mother's Prayer is described as a sacred prophecy of the Navi.
The prophecy dates back to the early times of the Navi's existence in Midgard and Atlas.
The Navi historically sought out the sons and daughters produced through the Mother's Prayer to aid their efforts in exploring Atlas.

Daisy.existing: Small girl who has previously appeared around Gerk and is associated with white flowers.
notes: Gerk again brings up Daisy as a small girl who has been following or appearing around him.
The DM says he has heard Gerk mention Daisy several times but has never personally seen her.
Gerk claims Daisy has previously stopped time without anyone else noticing.
Daisy's identity and connection to Gerk remain unexplained.
quotesThemes: Daisy is associated with unexplained supernatural events around Gerk.
openQuestions: How is Daisy connected to Gerk and the Mother's Prayer?
How is Daisy able to stop time without others noticing?

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric and the most knowledgeable member of the group.
notes: Chooses to follow Gerk as he takes up the role of the chosen child.
States that if Gerk has been chosen, there must be a purpose and she will go wherever he goes.
personality: Demonstrates loyalty to Gerk and willingness to trust the significance of his selection.
quotesThemes: Dana's decision emphasizes loyalty to Gerk and faith that his selection has a greater purpose.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter; Glimmen is his mind-linked dragon.
notes: Learns that Gerk is the chosen child and initially admits that he did not understand the significance of the Great Tree.
Is offered the opportunity to join Gerk's entourage and become connected to the chosen child and Great Tree.
personality: Reacts to the revelation with surprise and humor while remaining interested in joining Gerk's path.

notes: Glimmen is present through Walker's mind-linked perspective during the revelation about Gerk.
Was involved in the discussion concerning information previously revealed through the sitting stones and the Navi's plans.
Had previously withheld some information because the Navi appeared to have plans for the person involved.
personality: Shows caution about revealing information connected to the Navi before understanding its significance.

Plymouth Gawater.existing: Gnome artificer and friend of the party.
notes: Explains that Gerk's companions can potentially become metaphorical brothers and sisters of the chosen child of the Great Tree.
Appears to understand more about the Great Tree and its relationship to Gerk than Walker initially does.
Sylan references having gone through the sitting stones when discussing information connected to the Navi and another person's role.

misTranscriptions.notes: The campaign's established term is 'keystones', the physical stones associated with opening realm doors.
Lith is an established realm of Atlas; the transcript context makes the realm name likely.
Appears to be a name or term used while Gerk questions whether many people could fit the prophecy's description; insufficient context to identify it confidently.
Likely a proper noun for an established object or location, but this spelling should be confirmed.
The DM immediately corrects from a mistaken reference to Glimmen to Plymouth, the known gnome artificer.
The DM self-corrects the name while addressing Ciri.
The DM is speaking directly to Gerk in this scene.
Variant ASR rendering of Gerk's name.

openQuestions: Who is the originator or seer behind the Mother's Prayer?
What exactly is the role Gerk must take up as the chosen child?
What are the difficult choices that the Mother's Prayer foretells for Gerk?
What happens when the current growing season ends and the Great Tree produces another bud?
Who is Daisy, and what is her connection to Gerk and the Mother's Prayer?
How is Daisy able to stop time without anyone else noticing?

newTerms.name: Mother's Tales
notes: Alternate name used for the written or recorded versions of the Mother's Prayer.
Different tomes have been written by different authors, and some accounts can apparently rewrite themselves.

newTerms.name: Chosen Child of the Mother's Prayer
notes: The individual produced by the Mother's Prayer who becomes the hero at the center of its prophetic cycle.
Gerk is explicitly confirmed as the current chosen child.

newTerms.name: Sons and Daughters of the Great Tree
notes: Individuals associated with the Mother's Prayer and its Great Tree lineage.
The DM says Gerk is one of these sons and daughters and that several have existed historically.

newTerms.name: Mother's Prayer Growing Season
notes: A metaphorical cycle associated with the Mother's Prayer and Great Tree.
The current growing season is nearing its end, after which the tree is expected to sprout another bud.

newTerms.name: Chosen Child's Entourage
notes: Gerk's companions may voluntarily join him as part of his entourage.
Joining appears to establish a familial or kinship-like relationship to the chosen child and Great Tree.

newTerms.name: Sitting Stones
notes: An object or location previously used by the party in connection with information involving the Navi.
The exact nature of the Sitting Stones is not established in this chunk.
